iWant: Finalise to check test strength and Code Nodes for every touched criterion, and that the round declared every criterion it changed
soThat: a round cannot slip a changed criterion past the mutation proof or ship a vacuous test
description: Slice-scope checks and the separation audit inside Finalise.
title: The stage-keeper sees Finalise refuse unless test strength, touched criteria, Code Nodes and separation all hold

acceptanceCriteria.description: [failure] Given the happy fixture with no test-strength record at H, Finalise exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: no test-strength record at <H7>"; with a record whose AC-101-2 result is fail, it exits 4 with "finalise refused: test-strength at <H7> fails for AC-101-2"; with a record covering AC-101-1 only, it exits 4 with "finalise refused: test-strength at <H7> omits AC-101-2".

[failure] Given the happy fixture where the ReviewVerdict touches only AC-101-1 but the DEFINE: commit of the round changed AC-101-2's then text (or added a test case bound to AC-101-2), Finalise exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: touched criteria omit AC-101-2 changed since <base7>".

[failure] Given the happy fixture with no --ci-run, Finalise exits 4 with stderr "ci evidence missing: pass --ci-run <ref>"; given AC-101-2 with no Code Node, it exits 3 with "finalise refused: missing Code Node for AC-101-2"; a criterion of FBS-001 that the round did not touch and that has no Code Node does not refuse (slice scope).

[failure] Given the happy fixture plus an earlier "BUILD: tests" commit in the range touching test/rcf/a.test.js, Finalise exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: separation FAIL: <s7> BUILD: touches test/rcf/a.test.js (class rcfTest, owned by DEFINE)"; a range carrying a Hand: mixed commit refuses the same way with the audit's retired-mixed item, and Finalise never lists a separation exception as acceptable.

[must-not] Finalise never re-runs the suite, test strength or the separation audit as a child process and never spawns anything but git: a spawn seam over the happy run records only git, and the separation judgement runs in-process over git output.
